import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
spending_cols = [
    'MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts',
    'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'
]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Drop rows where Income is NaN, as it's a key variable for this visualization
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    s=70,              # Size of the markers
    alpha=0.7,         # Transparency to show density in overlapping areas
    edgecolor='w',     # White edge around markers for better distinction
    linewidth=0.5      # Line width of the marker edge
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Total Customer Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Income (€)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products (€)', fontsize=14)

# Customize the legend
plt.legend(title='Education Level', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11',

# Add a grid for better readability

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
